title: Winged bean Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Winged bean Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Winged bean nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of phosphorus and nitrogen in sigarilyas, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Winged bean nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your sigarilyas (winged bean) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are phosphorus, nitrogen, potassium, calcium and molybdenum. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Phosphorus deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for winged bean

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Phosphorus, nitrogen, potassium and molybdenum move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which winged bean nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a winged bean nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest winged bean nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Phosphorus deficiency in winged bean
Vines grow slowly and stay short, leaves are dark green, and pods and tubers are few. Nodules form poorly and fix little nitrogen. You see it most at this stage: early growth to flowering.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in sigarilyas
Red, acid, phosphorus poor soils. Okinawa trials found poor growth there came from phosphorus shortage, not from acidity, and lime alone did not help.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency makes vines pale. Waterlogging also stunts plants, with yellow leaves. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus before planting.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer such as 16 20 0, Complete 14 14 14 or Superphosphate 0 18 0 at planting, following the soil test. Phosphorus fed vines grew much better than limed ones in the Okinawa trials.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting rows each season.
Nitrogen deficiency in winged bean

Lower leaves pale and yellow and the vine stays light green and slow. Winged bean gets its nitrogen from root nodules, so pale vines usually mean the nodules are few or not working. Low phosphorus and potassium also cut nodule activity. You see it most at this stage: three to six weeks after planting.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in sigarilyas

In a legume this usually means poor nodulation: no inoculant in a field new to the crop, inoculant killed by sun or heat, very acid soil, waterlogging, hot dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer near the seed, which stops nodules from forming. In winged bean, low phosphorus and potassium also reduce nitrogen fixation.
How to tell it apart

Phosphorus shortage stunts the vine but keeps leaves dark. Sulfur deficiency yellows the young leaves first. To be sure, dig, do not pull, a few plants 3 to 6 weeks after planting, wash the roots and cut some nodules open. Pink to red inside means they are working, white means not active yet, and brown, grey or mushy means dead.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Feed the vines with a light sidedress of Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14, following the soil test. Correct phosphorus and potassium so the nodules can work.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, inoculate seed with a cowpea group Rhizobium inoculant, keep it shaded, and fertilize with phosphorus and potassium at planting.
Potassium deficiency in winged bean

Older leaves yellow or scorch at the margins, starting on the lower leaves. A Brazilian study found potassium, like phosphorus, strongly raised nitrogen fixation in winged bean, so short vines and pale leaves can follow. You see it most at this stage: mid growth to pod filling.
Why potassium deficiency happens in sigarilyas
Sandy and highly weathered soils and fields cropped without potash.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium deficiency yellows between the veins. To be sure, soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Complete 14 14 14 following the soil test.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash at planting and return vines to the soil.
Calcium deficiency in winged bean
Terminal buds and roots fail to develop, so the vine tips stall and roots stay short. Added calcium raised nitrogen fixation in winged bean trials. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why calcium deficiency happens in sigarilyas
Very acid soils, usually below pH 5, low in organic matter.
How to tell it apart
Boron deficiency also kills growing tips but crinkles young leaves. To be sure, soil pH and calcium test.
What to apply for calcium deficiency
Apply Agricultural lime or Dolomite on acid soils, or Gypsum where pH is fine, following the soil test.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, test the soil and lime well ahead of planting if it is very acid.
Molybdenum deficiency in winged bean

Vines are pale and small, just like nitrogen deficiency, because nodules need molybdenum to fix nitrogen. In some vegetables the leaf edges brown and cup upward. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why molybdenum deficiency happens in sigarilyas
Acid, sandy and highly weathered soils, where molybdenum is held tightly.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency from poor inoculation looks the same. Check the soil pH. To be sure, soil pH test and a look at the nodules.
What to apply for molybdenum deficiency
Liming to pH 6.0 or above often fixes it (UW). Otherwise treat seed with about 35 g of molybdenum per hectare, or spray about 140 to 210 g of sodium or ammonium molybdate per hectare.

Sold here with molybdenum: **Tierramino Molybdenum** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (16 percent molybdenum), **YaraVita Teprosyn Mo** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (15 percent P2O5 and 15.3 percent molybdenum), **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate General Purpose** by Sagrex Corporation (2 percent Fe, 0.5 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 3 percent S with Cu, Zn, B, Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [molybdenum deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/molybdenum-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime very acid soils before planting legumes.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any winged bean nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your sigarilyas needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Winged bean nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my sigarilyas leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: pale, slow vines whose roots have few pink nodules. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at potassium deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in winged bean?
items.a: Apply a phosphorus fertilizer such as 16 20 0, Complete 14 14 14 or Superphosphate 0 18 0 at planting, following the soil test. Phosphorus fed vines grew much better than limed ones in the Okinawa trials.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in winged bean?
items.a: Feed the vines with a light sidedress of Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14, following the soil test. Correct phosphorus and potassium so the nodules can work.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in winged bean?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Complete 14 14 14 following the soil test.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my sigarilyas lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the winged bean nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
